summary: Charlestown, NH tower work on Sam's Hill reported under way in July 1939; listed as gone; no source read describes the summit today.

facts.status_note: firelookout.org lists the tower as gone; no source read describes what remains on the summit

events.note: July 1939 Springfield Register item: road to the top completed and work to establish a fire lookout tower under way (reported, not confirmed as finished)

evidence.supports: road to the top of Sam's Hill reported completed and tower work going on
evidence.quote: We understand the road to the top of Sam's Hill has been completed, and that the work to establish a fire lookout tower there is going on a pace.

evidence.supports: workmen were busy on hurricane cleanup earlier in the week of June 25, 1939, clearing combustible material
evidence.quote: several automobile loads of workmen were busy in this section on hurricane work, cleaning up inflammable material

evidence.supports: the hill was not named for Sam Smith, who lived in the locality later
evidence.quote: Sam's Hill was not named for this Sam, but many years ago, before Mr. Smith lived in this locality

evidence.supports: Sams Hill listed among mountains which once had a fire tower, 1,683 feet, Charlestown
the list is headed as mountains which once had a fire tower
evidence.quote: Mountains which Once Had a Fire Tower

evidence.supports: firelookout.org lists the Sam's Hill tower as gone

sources.title: Fire Tower History - NH Family Hikes

notes_for_editor: Thin record: the only dated source is the July 1939 newspaper item, reported through Forest Lookouts, and it says the road was complete and tower work was moving along, not that a tower was finished. No completion date, removal date, or current site description was found in sources that could be read. Unverified lead: a geocache page (geocaching.com/geocache/GCA9GTB, created 2023) names a Sams Hill Fire Tower and a trail on top; its body text did not load in fetch_text, and the search snippet only was seen. The NH state PDF forest-lookout-towers-history.pdf returned 403. The story runs short because the evidence is thin; it should not be padded. Access is not recorded because no source describes it.
